content: Kodi plugin invocations and xbmc.service add-ons run as separate CPython sub-interpreters inside ONE Kodi OS process, on separate threads. Python-level primitives (threading.Lock, module globals) are NOT shared between them. The conventional cross-invocation channel is xbmcgui.Window(10000) (the Home window) setProperty/getProperty/clearProperty - a C++-backed string map shared by every interpreter, in-memory, no disk IO. It has no atomic test-and-set, so it is a cache/signal, not a mutex. POSIX fcntl record locks are per-process and therefore do NOT mutually exclude two sub-interpreters of the same Kodi process; an atomic os.open(path, O_CREAT|O_EXCL) lock file with a stale timeout is the portable cross-interpreter mutex that also works on Windows and Android.
